label: mid-input o/a/f/p/u after h/1/j/0/z context (diffuse)
explanation: Fires almost only while the original tokens are being read (91% of mass) and at <DEL> (9%), and almost never during copy. It peaks at t=3-6 and never fires at t=0-1. Rate depends on the current token (o 7.8x, then a, f, p, u) and on the earlier context: it is higher when h, 1, j, 0 or z appeared before (first_tok h 4.6x, prev2_tok j/0/1/h about 4x) and when the input has more digits. The strongest activations are o or a right after a prefix full of h/j/0/1. The best conjunction (current token in o/a/f/p/u and at least two earlier h/1/j/0/z) only reaches dev F1 0.32 and mass recall 0.39. Many activations fall on other tokens (r, m, 0, x, <DEL>), and many o/a in matching contexts stay silent. This reads as a distributed, context-weighted unit with no clean boolean description.
